title: CRLA/246/2017 of Sudha Sharma Alias Priyanshu Alias Inku Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No. 230 of 2017

Yogesh @ Muli ....Appellant
Versus
State ....Respondent
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. K.R. Gazi, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Amit Bhatt, Dy.A.G. for the State.
With
Criminal Appeal No. 246 of 2017

Sudha Sharma ....Appellant
Versus
State ....Respondent
Mr. B.C. Pande, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. H.C. Pathak, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Amit Bhatt, Dy.A.G. for the State.
Judgment Reserved- 06.03.2018
Date of Judgment - 20.03.2018
Coram: Hon'ble Rajiv Sharma, J.
 Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Per: Hon'ble Rajiv Sharma, J.
 Since common questions of law and facts are
involved in the above titled appeals, hence the same are
being taken up together and adjudicated by this common
judgment.
2. These appeals are directed against the judgment
and order dated 27.07.2017, rendered by learned IV
Additional Sessions Judge, Haridwar in Sessions Trial
No.278 of 2011, whereby the appellants were charged with
and tried for the offences under Section 302 and 120-B
IPC. The appellants were convicted and sentenced to
undergo rigorous life imprisonment and to pay of fine of
Rs.50,000/- each under Section 302 IPC and in default of
payment of fine to undergo additional two years' rigorous
imprisonment. The appellants were further convicted and
sentenced to undergo rigorous life imprisonment and to pay
a fine of Rs.50,000/- each under Section 120-B IPC and in

2
default of payment of fine to undergo additional two years'
rigorous imprisonment. All the sentences were ordered to
run concurrently.
3. The case of the prosecution, in a nutshell, is that
on 23.04.2011 at about 8:50 PM, Vinod Prasad Gairola has
filed a report to the effect that on 21.04.2011 at about
09:35 PM, husband and wife have stayed in the hotel. The
wife has produced her ID. They were allotted Room No.203.
When waiter went to served them tea, the door was locked.
They started peeping in the room. The person who stayed
with the lady has died. Prakash Sharma, father of the
deceased, also lodged the report to the effect that on
24.04.2011 telephonic call was received in Bhag Singh's
STD. One female has given information that Sudhir Pandit
was found murdered in Himalaya Hotel, Haridwar. He
sought further information. His nephew got the information
from the internet. The news item had appeared in daily
edition of Dainik Jagran newspaper that a boy was killed.
He along with the nephew Vinit Kumar Sharma, Rishi
Kumar Sharma and Dev Dutt Sharma came to Haridwar.
He recognized the photographs of his son. His son had
stayed with the appellant-Sudha Sharma. She killed his
son in the intervening night of 22-23.04.2011. On
20.04.2011 at about 11:00 PM, his son had gone to sleep
with his family. His son received call from the appellant-Yogesh. He tried to hear the conversation. He heard the
names of Yogesh @ Muli and Sudha from the mouth of his
son. On 21.04.2011, his son asked for Rs.5,000/- from him
to see his sister. He gave him Rs.5,000/-. His son, instead
of visiting his sister, went to Haridwar with appellant-Sudha Sharma. The FIR was registered. The dead body was
sent for postmortem examination. The postmortem
examination was conducted by PW6 Ved Prakash Maurya.

3
The matter was investigated and the challan was put up
after completing all the codal formalities.
4. The prosecution has examined number of
witnesses in its support. The statements of the appellants
were also recorded under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. They have
denied the case of the prosecution.
5. The appellants were convicted and sentenced as
noticed hereinabove. Hence, these appeals.
6. Learned Senior Advocates for the appellants have
vehemently argued that the prosecution has failed to prove
its case against the appellants beyond reasonable doubt.
7. Learned Counsel for the State has supported the
judgment and order dated 27.07.2017.
8. We have heard learned counsel for both the
parties and perused the judgment and record carefully.
9. PW1 Prakash Sharma is the father of the
deceased. According to him, his son Sudhir was 38 years
old. He was married. He has five children. He used to assist
him in selling tea. Appellant- Sudha Sharma was the sister-in-law of his son. He developed illicit relations with
appellant-Sudha Sharma. His son left him and went to the
house of appellant-Yogesh @Muli at Kela Vihar, Ghaziabad.
He stayed there for 3-4 months. Sudhir used to work.
Appellant-Yogesh used to visit Sudha Sharma. Appellant-Sudha Sharma developed illicit realations with Yogesh.
Sudhir came to know about it. He scolded appellant-Sudha
Sharma. He gave beatings to her. Appellant-Sudha Sharma
told this fact to Yogesh. Thereafter, they left the house. The
house was locked. Sudhir came in the evening. Sudhir
came back to his family. All these incidents were narrated
to him by the Advocate. On 20.04.2011, his son received a
telephonic call at 11:00 PM from appellant-Yogesh. He

4
overheard the conversation. On 21.04.2011, Sudhir asked
for Rs.5,000/- from him to visit his sister. Thereafter, he
received a message in the STD of Bhag Singh. He reached
the police station. He recognized the photographs. In his
cross-examination, he has deposed that he has asked his
son to mend his ways. They came to know about the illicit
relations of his son through in-laws of his son.
10. PW2 Dev Dutt Sharma has deposed that he knew
Sudhir Sharma. He was married 18 years back. Sudhir
Sharma developed illicit relations with his sister-in-law. He
went to Ghaziabad. Sudhir Sharma developed friendship
with appellant-Yogesh. Sudhir and Sudha were taken by
Yogesh to his house in Village Kela Dehat. Sudhir used to
work in a company. Yogesh developed illicit relations with
appellant- Sudha Sharma. Sudhir came back to his house.
He came to Himalaya Hotel and recognized the appellant-Sudha Sharma and Sudhir with the help of photographs.
He has seen the CCTV footage between 21.04.2011 to
23.04.2011. He has seen the photographs of Sudha
Sharma dated 21.04.2011 at 09:30 PM and Yogesh dated
22.04.2011 at 08:30 PM.
11. PW3 Vinod Prasad Gairola has testified that he
was working in Himalaya Hotel as Waiter. The couple had
come to the hotel on 21.04.2011. Room No.203 was allotted
to them. The order was placed with Deepak to bring two
cups of tea at 08:00 AM. The woman had come to the
reception to get medicine for her husband. At 08:00 AM,
Deepak took tea. The door was locked. They peeped into the
room. The person who had stayed in the hotel was found
dead.
12. PW4 Rishi Sharma has not supported the case of
the prosecution. He was declared hostile.

5
13. PW5 Deepak is the waiter. According to him,
PW3 Vinod Prasad Gairola was the manager of the hotel.
The couple had come on 21.04.2011 at 09:25 PM. The room
was allotted to them. He has given food in Room No.203. He
was asked to bring tea at 08:00 AM. When he went to the
room, it was locked. He informed the manager. Thereafter,
they peeped into the room. The person who was staying in
the room with the lady was found dead.
14. PW6 Dr. Ved Prakash Maurya has conducted the
postmortem examination. According to him, the deceased
died due to shock and hemorrhage due to ante mortem
injuries. He proved the postmortem report.
15. PW7 Preetpal Singh Rautela is the Investigating
Officer initially. He has recovered blood stained knife.
16. PW9 Sabal Chand has deposed that he has
lodged the FIR at the instance of Vinod Prasad Gairola. In
his cross-examination, he has admitted that the person
who has lodged the report has not given the details of
register and voter ID. The CCTV footage was also not
handed over.
17. PW10 Revti @ Anuj. His statement was recorded
under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. He has not
supported the case of the prosecution. He was declared
hostile.
18. PW11 A.S.I. Vidhya Bhusan Singh Negi is the
formal witness.
19. PW12 Inspector Mahendra Singh Negi. He has
recorded the statement of PW10 Rewti @ Anuj under
Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. They interrogated PW10
Revti. PW10 Revti told them during the course of
interrogation that on 21.04.2011 appellant-Yogesh had
come to him and asked him to go towards Haridwar. They

6
went to Haridwar on 22.04.2011 at 10:00 AM. They took
bath in Ganges and went to the Himalaya Hotel. They were
allotted Room No.304. Yogesh consumed liquor. Thereafter,
appellant-Yogesh went out and came back and asked him
to leave the hotel.
20. The case of the prosecution is based entirely on
circumstantial evidence. In order to prove the case based
on circumstantial evidence, it is necessary to complete the
entire chain. All the circumstances must point out
exclusively towards the guilt of the accused.
21. The case of the prosecution is that appellant-Sudha Sharma developed illicit relations with the deceased.
Thereafter, she developed illicit relations with appellant-Yogesh. Sudhir and appellant-Sudha Sharma came to
Haridwar and stayed in Himalaya hotel. On 21.04.2011,
she killed Sudhir with the help of appellant-Yogesh.
Appellant-Sudha Sharma, and Sudhir were staying in
Room No.203 and appellant- Yogesh with his friend was
staying in Room No.304. The cause of death of the
deceased was shock and hemorrhage as a result of ante
mortem injuries. The post mortem report was prepared by
PW6 Dr. Ved Prasad Gairola.
22. PW1 Prakash Sharma has categorically deposed
that his son had developed illicit relations with appellant-Sudha Sharma. Appellant-Sudha Sharma was the sister-in-law of his son. He went to Ghaziabad. Thereafter, he met
the appellant-Yogesh. He stayed in the house of Yogesh.
Thereafter, appellant-Sudha Sharma developed illicit
relations with appellant-Yogesh. His son scolded Sudha
Sharma. Appellant-Sudha Sharma told this fact to
appellant-Yogesh. Thereafter, Sudhir left the house. Sudhir
came back to his family. According to PW1 Prakash
Sharma, these incidents were told to him by Advocate, who

7
was his neighbour. How the advocate could know about
these incidents is beyond comprehension. He has neither
any communication with the appellant(s) nor with the
father of the deceased. PW1 Prakash Sharma has also
deposed that they came to know about the illicit relations of
his son with appellant-Sudha Sharma through the in-laws
of his son. No member of the family of in-laws of his son
was examined by the prosecution. According to him, his
son received a telephonic call on 20.04.2011 from Yogesh.
He overheard the conversation. Sudhir told the incidents to
his mother and wife. Neither mother nor wife were
examined by the prosecution. PW1 Prakash Sharma has
lodged the report and not said anything about the illicit
relations between the appellant-Sudha Sharma and his
son. This is serious omission.
23. PW2 Devdutt Sharma. According to him also, the
appellant-Sudha Sharma developed illicit relations with
Sudhir. He has recognized Sudhir with the help of
photographs. He has seen the CCTV footage of Sudha
Sharma on 21.04.2011 at 09:30 PM and of appellant-Yogesh on 22.04.2011 at 08:30 PM. The police has not
taken into possession the CCTV footage. He has
categorically admitted that he came to know about the
illicit relations of Sudhir with appellant-Sudha Sharma on
hearsay. He had no personal knowledge about the illicit
relations of appellant-Sudha Sharma with Sudhir.
24. PW3 Vinod Prasad Gairola has been shown to be
the employee of the Himalaya Hotel. According to him,
Room No.203 was allotted to the appellant-Sudha Sharma
and the deceased. According to him, appellant-Sudha
Sharma and Sudhir had given order to PW5 Deepak to
bring tea in the morning on 21.04.2011 at 08:00 AM. But
in fact, the death has occurred in the intervening night of
22-23.04.2011. PW3 Vinod Prasad Gairola did not know

8
the direction of the main door of the hotel, the direction of
the counter of the hotel. He did not know the direction of
the door of Room No.203. In case, he has worked in the
hotel, he should have known about the exact location of the
main door, the counter and the direction of the door of
Room No.203.
25. PW4 Rishi Sharma has not at all supported the
case of the prosecution. He was declared hostile.
26. PW5 Deepak Singh has deposed that appellant-Sudha Sharma and the deceased were given Room No.203.
The lady, after taking dinner, had gone out on 22.04.2011
and did not come back. He has seen the dead body of
Sudhir by peeping into the door. The police has taken into
possession the shoes and also two bottles of liquor. The
photographs were taken from CCTV footage. However, the
CCTV footage was not produced.
27. PW7 Preetipal Singh Rautela was the
Investigating Officer initially. He investigated the matter. In
his cross-examination, he has categorically admitted that
he has not taken into possession the CCTV footage. He has
not lifted the fingerprints of the accused. The call details
were not proved as per the law. He did not know the name
of the person who has prepared the photographs from
CCTV footage. He has not made inqiry with regard to the ID
produced by the appellant-Sudha Sharma.
28. PW8 Baru Singh Chauhan has recorded the
statement of Leelawati. He did not remember the G.D.
number at the time when he departed from the office. He
has not produced any record of Ghaziabad police station.
29. PW9 Sabal Singh Chauhan has deposed that at
the time when the FIR was registered, neither the details of
register nor voter ID was provided.

9
30. PW10 Revti @ Anuj has not supported the case of
the prosecution. Though, his statement was recorded under
Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. for his caution.
31. PW11 Vidhya Bhushan Negi is the formal
witness.
32. PW12 Inspector Mahendra Singh has deposed
the manner, in which PW10 Revti @ Anuj has met the
appellant-Yogesh and came with him to Haridwar and
stayed in Room No.304. PW10 Revti @ Anuj has resiled
from his statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of
Cr.P.C.
33. There is no eye-witness. The case is based on
circumstantial evidence, though PW2 Dev Dutt Sharma has
deposed that he has seen the photographs. The
photographs were prepared from the CCTV footage. The
CCTV footage was not produced on record. PW10 Revti @
Anuj, who had allegedly accompanied Yogesh to Haridwar
has not supported the case of the prosecution and was
declared hostile.
34. DW1 Dinesh Chandra Sharma has deposed that
he has never given any house on rent to appellant-Yogesh.
35. DW2 Chote Lal has deposed that neither in the
house of Yogesh nor in the house of his uncle, Sudhir and
appellant-Sudha Sharma has ever stayed.
36. The prosecution has not led any tangible
evidence to prove that appellant-Sudha Sharma developed
illicit relations with deceased. According to PW1 Prakash
Sharma, deceased-Sudhir has told about the threats
advanced to him by Yogesh to his mother and wife. Neither
mother nor wife were examined by the prosecution. No
person from the in-laws of his son has been examined to
prove illicit relations between appellant-Sudha Sharma and

10
Sudhir. PW1 Prakash Sharma has not stated anything
about the illicit relations of the appellant-Sudha Sharma
and Sudhir in the complaint filed by him in the police
station. PW2 Dev Dutt Sharma has admitted that he has no
personal knowledge of the illicit relations of Sudhir and
Sudha Sharma. His information was based on hearsay. It is
also not believable how father would hear the conversation
on phone received by his son from Yogesh on 20.01.2011 at
11:00 PM. PW3 Vinod Prasad Gairola did not know the
topography of the hotel. His presence in the hotel is
doubtful. PW3 Vinod Prasad Gairola has deposed that the
waiter was sent to serve tea on 21.04.2011 at 08:00 AM but
in fact, the date of death was the intervening night of
22/23.04.2011. PW1 Prakash Sharma has deposed that his
neighbour-advocate has told him about the incidents. The
advocate was not supposed to know his son's illicit
relations with his sister-in-law and he is going to
Ghaziabad.
37. The prosecution has relied upon the photocopy
of register whereby the entry of the appellant-Yogesh along
with his friend was made. The prosecution has not
produced the original register on the plea that it was
destroyed in rain. It is the secondary evidence. It was
required to be proved in accordance with law. The
prosecution has not proved call details as per Section 65-B
of the Indian Evidence Act. The police, though, recovered
the knife, but it was not sent for FSL examination. There is
no FSL report on record.
38. The prosecution has failed to prove its case
against the appellants beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, these criminal appeals are allowed and the
judgment and order dated 27.07.2017, rendered by IV
Additional Sessions Judge, Haridwar is set-aside. The
appellants are acquitted of the charges framed against

11
them. The appellants are in jail. Let they be released
forthwith, if not required in connection with any other
matter.
39. Let a copy of this judgment along with LCR be sent
back to the trial court.
 (Alok Singh, J.) (Rajiv Sharma, J.)
NISHANT
